citations.title: Research Statement Languages, Compilers, and Tools for Multicore Architectures

reception: Within the polyhedral compilation literature the framework became part of the standard background: works on automatic parallelization, AlphaZ, and the Sparse Polyhedral Framework cite it in passing when surveying affine scheduling and memory optimization. The engaged reception is narrower and mathematical. Darte and Schreiber's lattice-based memory allocation examines the occupancy-vector formulation in detail, and Touati and Eisenbeis carried the joint schedule–storage view into periodic register allocation on ILP processors, with later work adopting the formulation for periodic task scheduling with storage minimization; a study of LLM-guided loop optimization returned to its examples as benchmarks. The citations are not numerous, but those that engage do so with the mathematics.
